newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BOE, NBS Boland join forces.
newsitem.headline: BOE, NBS Boland join forces.

text.p: NBS Holdings, Boland Bank Holdings and the Board of Executors have joined forces to create South Africa's fifth largest banking group while retaining their separate identities.
BOE announced on Thursday that it had bought 22.2 percent of NBS shares at 68.35 cents each or a total of 1.37 billion rand, while NBS Boland had bought 24.3 percent of BOE for 880 million rand.
After the merger of NBS and Boland, BOE's shareholding will fall to 17.2 percent of the enlarged group.
BOE's acquisition has been financed through the private placement of shares with major institutions, which was heavily oversubscribed and had to be scaled back.

The other major shareholder in NBS Boland is Samgro Investment Holdings Ltd, the pyramid company of Boland Bank headed by Christo Wiese, which will own 15 percent after the merger, with rights to take up another 19 percent to take its shareholding up to 34.9 percent.

NBS Boland said in a statement that its acquisition of the stake in BOE would not affect the merger between NBS and Boland Bank, which goes into effect on May 1, and the three institutions would operate as autonomous units under their own brand names.
The deal follows the sale by NBS of its interest in Norwich Holdings for 625 million rand and in Aegis for 135 million rand.

BOE executive chairman Bill McAdam said the NBS Boland acquisition would have a dramatic effect on BOE. Assuming the association had been in place for the year to the end of September 1996, attributable profits would have risen 177 percent to 171.7 milion rand.
BOE managing director Phil Biden said that the deal would lead to major cross-selling opportunities for the two groups.
"This is not an acquisition for getting big and influential. In our view it makes extremely good business sense," McAdam said.

"We have always run this company on the basis of adding value on a per share basis. The financial impact of this transaction for us is huge but I think that for fundamental business reasons and the potential for crossflow... makes the next five to six years in this very exciting."
"In BOE we have a partner with the shared desire of being a top performer in the financial services market," NBS Boland chairman Cedric Savage said.
"It also brings with it a well-established international partnership with NatWest, the world's fifth largest bank, which can be developed further to our mutual benefit."

BOE also announced that it had raised a further 327.7 million rand through share placements for cash. This would be used for potential acquistions in its core activities of private banking, asset management, life assurance and merchant and investment banking as well as occasional strategic investments.
The new BOE shares have been placed by BOE Natwest Ltd with institutional investors at 90 rand a share, with 50 percent being taken up by BOE Corporation BOE's holding company.
